proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original final sentence asserted that any failure to separate an HSIC interval necessarily produces more than one terminal graph. An ambiguous score-only functional, or an ambiguity shared by paths that prune to the same graph, need not change the graph union. The valid honest conclusion is that both labels and all compatible terminal DAGs are retained; the resulting set may or may not be a singleton.

proposed.statement: Every law in \(\mathcal M_0(d)\) identifies \(G_0\). Support closure first makes the structural recursion a law on \(\mathcal X\). On every nonempty conditional-support fiber, the induced density is positive and three times continuously differentiable on a connected relative interior. The conditional-independence intersection argument therefore applies on that open set, connectedness rules out patching distinct reverse factorizations across disjoint interior components, and the support boundary is null. Assumption \(\ref{ass:condition19-configurations}\) then supplies an interior open set on which Peters et al.'s differential identity fails, excluding every reversed bivariate conditional ANM. These steps extend their positive-density Condition 19 argument to the stated compact-support regime without assuming uniqueness of the DAG.
proposed.justification: The compact-domain model needs a genuine identification bridge because positivity only on relative interiors is weaker than full-support positivity.
proposed.gap: Peters et al. (2014, Condition 19, Definition 27, and Theorem 28) do not state the support-closed compact-fiber extension.
proposed.consumer: The score analysis can target the labelled DAG using a proved compact restricted-ANM identification result.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the published restricted-ANM identification theorem as the cited leaf used by the compact-support adaptation.

proposed.statement: Let \((G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\). For every \(\pi\notin\Pi(G_0)\), choose a component edge \(u\to v\) with \(v\) before \(u\) and insert \(u\) immediately before \(v\). This move belongs to \(\operatorname{Corr}_{G_0}(\pi)\) and satisfies \(C_P(\pi;r,s)\ge\rho^{\to}_{uv}-(d-1)\rho^{\leftarrow}_{uv}/d\ge\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}>0\). The bound follows from the structural product law: before the move the reversed root contributes at most \((d-1)\rho^{\leftarrow}_{uv}/d\), after the move the effect contributes \(\rho^{\to}_{uv}\), and every traversed node from another independent component has unchanged explained risk and a weakly larger GENE penalty factor. Consequently every insertion-local maximizer is topological.
proposed.justification: This is the field-level root result: a check on mechanisms and noise laws yields strict local ascent without assuming any ordering of permutation scores.
proposed.gap: Li et al. (2025, Theorem 4.3) assume a global ranking for every pair of orders with different ancestral-reversal counts and give no structural-function condition implying a correcting insertion.
proposed.consumer: Benchmark designers can certify population success of insertion search directly from each cause--effect module.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Add the variance and characteristic-kernel assumptions used explicitly in the gain calculation and reverse-dependence step.

proposed.statement: Li et al.'s global reversal-monotone premise implies the positive correcting-move property on the matching-component graph class, but the converse fails even for smooth identifiable ANMs. For all sufficiently small \(\sigma>0\), \(P_{\mathrm{sep},\sigma}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(6)\): symmetry gives \(\rho^{\leftarrow}_{12}=0\), while \(\rho^{\to}_{12}\to1\) and both directional ratios on edges \(3\to4\) and \(5\to6\) converge to \(1\). Nevertheless, for \(\pi_1=(2,3,4,5,6,1)\) and \(\pi_2=(1,2,4,6,3,5)\), \(\operatorname{Rev}_{G_0}(\pi_1)=1<2=\operatorname{Rev}_{G_0}(\pi_2)\), whereas \(S_{P_{\mathrm{sep},\sigma}}(\pi_1)\to2\) and \(S_{P_{\mathrm{sep},\sigma}}(\pi_2)\to1+4/5+5/6>2\). Continuity of the correlation ratios, together with forward residual independence and Condition 19 reverse dependence for every \(\sigma>0\), makes the reversed ranking strict for small positive \(\sigma\). Thus Theorem \(\ref{thm:pairwise-navigation}\) guarantees local recovery for a support-closed smooth law excluded by Li et al.'s premise.
proposed.justification: An explicit score-limit calculation certifies a strict reduction in the recovery hypothesis, rather than a verbal comparison between differently named conditions.
proposed.gap: Li et al. (2025, Theorem 4.3 and its proof on page 5) establish sufficiency of global reversal monotonicity but do not separate it from the local property their optimizer needs.
proposed.consumer: Users obtain a guarantee for heterogeneous modular systems whose inversion costs cannot be ranked by an unweighted reversal count.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the structural, variance, and conditional-functional nodes used to verify that the explicit six-node law belongs to the base class and to compute its score limits.

proposed.statement: For \(P_{\mathrm w,\sigma}\), the forward residual is independent of \(X\), the reverse conditional-mean residual is dependent on \(Y\), and, with \(m_2=\mathbb E[Z^2]\), \(C_{P_{\mathrm w,\sigma}}((Y,X);2,1)\ge1/2-\sigma^2m_2/\operatorname{Var}(X+X^2)\). Hence the correcting gain is positive for sufficiently small \(\sigma\) and converges to \(1/2\). The support-closure relation holds on \([0,1]\times[-\sigma,2+\sigma]\), and the Condition 19 differential identity fails on an interior open set.
proposed.justification: The witness supplies a quantitative, scale-invariant calibration of the primitive certificate in the smallest graph.
proposed.gap: Reisach et al. (2023, Sections 3 and 5) analyze normalized explained variance but not its combination with exact residual dependence in GENE Equation (6).
proposed.consumer: Implementers obtain an analytic two-node test case whose population gain approaches one half.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare characteristicness, which turns the proved reverse residual dependence into strict positive HSIC.

proposed.statement: If \((G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\), then \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{or}}(P,\pi)=G_0\) for every \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_I\). Strict ascent prevents revisiting an order, and Theorem \(\ref{thm:pairwise-navigation}\) makes every terminal order topological; Condition 19 configurations and causal minimality then make residual-independence pruning delete exactly the nonedges. The search uses at most \(d!-1\) insertions and \(d(d-1)d!\) gain comparisons. Memoization uses at most \(d2^{d-1}\) conditional-risk queries and \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\) score-relevant residual-HSIC queries, followed by at most \(d(d-1)/2\) pruning checks.
proposed.justification: The primitive certificate is useful only if it yields a complete labelled-DAG recovery theorem and a finite oracle budget.
proposed.gap: Solus, Wang, and Uhler (2021, Proposition 8 and Theorem 9) study covered-arrow walks for sparsity, while Li et al. (2025) do not give primitive risk and dependence query counts for GENE.
proposed.consumer: An implementation can cache the finite local-score table and know its worst-case population-query budget.
